- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope sharply and align with sentiment reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often ignores sentiment momentum; if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to reflect bullish momentum.
- If sentiment is flat or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to forecast mean of recent 7-day range; use 7-day moving average as baseline and adjust ±0.5% based on sentiment deviation.
